name: How to Handle an Emergency Roof Leak After a Storm in Alliance

step.name: Step 1: Prioritize Safety — First and foremost, make sure everyone in your Alliance home is safe and away from any immediate danger from the leak or storm damage. Avoid going onto the roof if it's wet, steep, or looks unstable, as this can be incredibly dangerous, especially right after a storm. Your personal safety is the most important thing to consider before anything else.

step.name: Step 2: Document the Damage (Safely) — Before you do anything else, if it's safe, take photos or videos of the leak and any visible damage, both inside and outside. This documentation is crucial for potential insurance claims and helps your roofing professional understand the situation better. Don't start any major cleanup or permanent repairs until you've documented the extent of the damage.

step.name: Step 3: Arrange for Temporary Protection — If water is actively coming into your home, your immediate goal is to prevent further damage. Use buckets, towels, or tarps to catch the water. If there's an exposed opening on your roof, you might need to arrange for temporary tarping or covering to prevent more water intrusion. This step is about limiting additional damage until professional help arrives.
